headline: Airbnb tops Q2 estimates, lifts 2026 outlook on strong travel demand
driver_sentence: For the third quarter, Airbnb forecast revenue of $4.69 billion ... It also forecast a full-year adjusted EBITDA margin of at least 35.5%.
notes: Corroborated by MarketScreener 7 Aug 2026 ("These results allowed Airbnb to raise its full-year targets: it now expects an adjusted EBITDA margin of at least 35.5% (rather than 35%)") and Barron's 7 Aug 2026 ("Airbnb Raises Guidance After Second-Quarter Earnings Beat"). Press leads with the raise, exactly as WS03 classified.

headline: Airbnb in top form after its summer results
driver_sentence: $1.26 expected by the consensus, along with adjusted EBITDA up 21%, to $1.26bn, [analyst]s on average were looking for around $1.23bn.
notes: Second source for the same print; also independently corroborates WS04's TIKR-derived $1,225.6m 2Q26 adjusted-EBITDA consensus.

headline: Airbnb shares jump on strong quarterly results, expansion plans
driver_sentence: Feb 14 (Reuters) - Airbnb shares rose as much as 13.3% in premarket trade on Friday [after strong quarterly results and expansion plans].
notes: Reuters' headline pairs the KPI beat with the 2025 expansion plans, which WS03's KPI class does not capture. Corroborated by "Airbnb Soars as Q4 Profits, Bookings Surge; Baird, Goldman Sachs Upgrade Outlook" (14 Feb 2025) - two same-day upgrades are part of the day-1 move and appear in neither WS03 nor WS04.

headline: Airbnb has best quarter on record, shares turn higher after hours
driver_sentence: Airbnb has best quarter on record, shares turn higher after hours
notes: Contemporaneous coverage leads with the record reported quarter, not the accelerating Q4 GBV guide that WS03 used as the driver quote. Indexed by Techmeme on 5 Nov 2021. WS03's own press_cited_driver text already mentions the record quarter first, so the mismatch is in the driver_class label only.

headline: What every Canadian investor needs to know today
driver_sentence: shares of Airbnb Inc. shares rose about 2 per cent in premarket trading after the company posted better-than-expected gross bookings in its [fourth quarter]
notes: MISMATCH. No contemporaneous outlet found attributes the +12.9% to the "30% EBITDA margins or greater" ambition WS03 quotes. Every same-day recap (CNBC $859m vs $748m; MarketWatch "sales held up better than expected"; IBD) attributes it to the revenue / gross-bookings beat and the reopening narrative. The margin quote is a plausible but unsourced attribution.

headline: Airbnb clocks first profitable year on strong travel demand
driver_sentence: Airbnb clocks first profitable year on strong travel demand
notes: The guide leg is explicit in the same-day recaps: T3 Live 15 Feb 2023, "Airbnb forecast Q1 revenue between $1.75 billion and $1.82 billion vs $1.68 billion expected." CNBC/NBC 15 Feb 2023: "the Nasdaq Composite rose 0.92%, boosted by shares of Airbnb, which surged 13.35% after beating earnings expectations." WS03's guide class is right; the profitability milestone is the co-driver.

headline: Airbnb forecasts lower third-quarter revenue as economic uncertainty weighs
driver_sentence: It expects third-quarter revenue to be between $3.67 billion and $3.73 billion, below analysts' estimate of $3.84 billion.
notes: IMPORTANT. Reuters' lede is the below-Street guide, not the macro sentence. This is also the source that fills WS04's single next-quarter consensus gap. CNBC's same-day headline ("Airbnb shares fall 14% on earnings miss, fear of slowing demand") supports the macro reading as the stated CAUSE, but the mechanism the market priced was a guide 3.6% below Street - the largest in the sample. WS03's 'macro' class should be 'guide, cause macro'.

headline: Stock market today: Dow ends lower as energy slips, but tech gains
driver_sentence: The company forecast bookings to grow more slowly than revenue in the second quarter
notes: Press frames the driver as the Q2 outlook, not the reported quarter. CNBC's midday-movers piece for 10 May 2023 uses the same framing ("second quarter and slower..."). Barron's weekend wrap (15 May 2023): "Airbnb shares fell after it beat...". The underlying fact is identical to WS03's quote; only the class label differs.

headline: Airbnb Shares Fall on Muted Fourth-Quarter Bookings Forecast
driver_sentence: Airbnb Shares Fall on Muted Fourth-Quarter Bookings Forecast
notes: Headline is unambiguous: the driver is the Q4 bookings FORECAST, i.e. the guide. WS03 classes it as KPI. Corroborated by The Globe and Mail market movers 2 Nov 2022 ("Airbnb Inc (ABNB-Q) forecast fourth-quarter ..."). Note the Fed hiked 75bp the same day (QQQ -3.4%), which WS03 already flags and the press does not.

headline: Airbnb's Revenue Tops Expectations, But Profits Fall Short
driver_sentence: Airbnb reported third-quarter revenue that beat expectations, but profits fell short.
notes: Press stops at "profits fell short" and "mixed financial results" (Yahoo Finance stock movers, 8 Nov 2024; StockStory "Why Airbnb (ABNB) Stock Is Trading Lower Today", 8 Nov 2024: "Overall, this was a mixed but weaker quarter"). No contemporaneous outlet located isolates S&M +27.5% / product development +25% as the driver. WS03's investment-spend reading is an analyst inference, defensible but not press-supported.

headline: Airbnb head for $5bn hit after Q2 warning
driver_sentence: Airbnb Inc (NASDAQ:ABNB, ETR:6Z1) shares fell nearly 7% in pre-market trading [after the Q2 warning]
notes: Corroborated by The Times business live blog 7 Aug 2025 ("Airbnb shares slide on slowdown") and Investopedia's 7 Aug 2025 market wrap ("Airbnb shares lost 8% on Thursday"). The 2H caution WS03 identifies is what the press calls the "warning"/"slowdown".
